neighbours.label: being in contact or company with other people: 'time with her guests', 'in touch with her friends', 'contact with the outside world' (fires on ' guests', ' contact', and the word after 'with'); the card's reflexive pronouns fire less reliably
fire: Grandmother baked all morning so she could sit and talk with her guests.
Even after retiring he kept in touch with his former colleagues.
During the quarantine the sailors had no contact with their families.
The bride barely had a moment to chat with her guests.
Living on the island, the monks avoided all contact with the outside world.
She moved to Canada but stays in touch with her cousins in Lisbon.
The innkeeper liked to share a glass of wine with his guests.
Since the quarrel he has lost contact with most of his old classmates.
quiet: Grandmother baked all morning so she could fill the tins with her biscuits.
Even after retiring he kept busy with his garden and his bees.
During the quarantine the sailors had no fresh fruit or vegetables.
The bride barely had a moment to look at her flowers.
Living on the island, the monks avoided all meat and strong drink.
She moved to Canada but keeps her savings in a bank in Lisbon.
The innkeeper liked to fill a glass of wine with his best vintage.
Since the quarrel he has lost interest in most of his old hobbies.

notes: Card: peak tokens ' themselves' x5, ' himself' x4, ' contact' x3, ' guests' x2; gate-closed regime dominates. Probes: 'spend time with her guests' 1.15, 'in touch with her old friends' 0.67, 'hate themselves' 0.57, 'contact with the outside world' 0.50, 'contact with his family' 0.42, ' visitors' 0.29; other reflexives ('washed themselves', 'blamed himself', 'give yourself') only 0.03-0.09, so the reflexive reading from the card did not hold up. The opposite pole is the token ' personally'.
